name: subordination
quote: I need to check with the boss.
description: The sense that specific actions or decisions are driven by someone or something besides yourself, but that you have chosen to comply.
perceptions: I'm constrained in certain actions and decisions by an agreement.
There may be consequences if I don't comply.
I've chosen to align myself with this person, group, or goal.
examples: Being bound by the company handbook.
Being constrained by the laws of your country and city

comparisons.description: 'Subordination' is the general concept that you can't just make any decision or take any fun action that you feel like at the moment. We are all constrained by agreements and goals with ourselves and with other people. 'Responsibility' is taking on a specific goal and aligning your actions to complete that goal instead of relaxing in front of the TV. 'Ownership' is taking on a large ill-defined set of goals that are required for some complex system to succeed. You need to figure out what to do and how to do not just one goal, but many. It's a hierarchy - the ship's captain has to own the whole voyage, deciding what needs to get done. These individual well-defined tasks become assigned responsibilities for crew members. Everyone is subordinate to someone or some goal, the difference being the scope of the goal.

commentaries.quote: Groups can work better if some individuals temporarily suppress their own agency so as to coordinate with others.
The principle of subordination is the great bond of union and harmony through the universe.
Sometimes you have to subordinate strategic considerations to tactical needs.
Always mistrust a subordinate who never finds fault with his superior.
